A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FAST study. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and the core method and experiments can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA, multimodal benchmark, segmentation, runtime, and ablation results in Tables 1–5, alongside qualitative successes and failures.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds an encoder comparison in Figure 4 and results separated by thinking mode in Appendix B, Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: v3 introduces an EVA2-CLIP-E encoder variant for the comparison in Figure 4, a limited model-component substitution. The switch, proposal, and segmentation adapters, Equations 1–7, and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure. The expanded resampler description documents an existing component.

E1.justification: The evaluation datasets and task families are unchanged, including those reused in the new thinking-mode breakdowns. Appendix A newly identifies PixelLM, VAW, and LLaVA-80K within training-data construction and describes generated multi-object questions. v1's less detailed account does not establish whether these represent additional training coverage or previously undisclosed constituents.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated comparisons with Chain of Spot, V*, and Visual CoT. Figure 4 additionally compares against CogCoM and a method labeled CoVLM, whose citation identifies CogVLM. This substantially expands comparison with other visual reasoning approaches. The original segmentation comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds an EVA2-CLIP-E comparison setting and evaluations separated into System 1 and System 2 subsets in Tables 6–7. Existing metrics, base configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged. The new encoder training settings and assignment of comparable mode subsets across methods are not fully specified.

E4.justification: New Appendix B compares FAST and baselines separately by thinking mode across four VQA datasets, refCOCOg, and ReasonSeg. This substantially extends v1's MME/GQA switching and runtime analysis by examining where mode-specific advantages occur across task families. The component ablations and qualitative failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1–5 retain their values, including FAST's 80.8 VQAv2 accuracy and 48.7 ReasonSeg GIoU. v3 adds comparator scores, encoder-variant results, and mode-specific findings; Table 6 reports System 2 GQA accuracy of 52.3 for FAST versus 50.7 for Chain of Spot. The GQA System 1 annotation changes from 78.8% in v1 Figure 4 to 70.2% in v3 Figure 5. The stronger-encoder results are additional settings, not same-setting version-to-version gains.

T1.justification: The definitions and mathematical pipeline in Equations 1–7 are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are introduced. The additional resampler explanation describes cross-attention without supplying a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: adaptive fast/slow switching, hierarchical chains of visual evidence, and an interpretable decision pipeline. The headline performance claims remain unchanged. Re-emphasizing neuro-symbolic reasoning does not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly interprets System 2 outcomes as combining fast reasoning on simpler subcomponents with slow reasoning on complex aspects. Appendix B adds broader generalization interpretations, and Appendix F contrasts FAST's efficiency and transparency with o1-style reasoning. v3 also removes v1's blanket assertion that context clues help less than missing objects, while retaining the original limitations and failure explanations.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands reproducibility information: learnable resampler queries and attention layers, InstructBLIP filtering, LaMa object removal, attribute-question construction, noun/category matching, and GPT-4/GPT-4V generation with an example prompt. These largely document previously underspecified construction steps. The abstract also supplies a public code-repository link, whereas v1 supplied an anonymous review link and release promise.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including CogCoM, PixelLM, EVA-CLIP, and several agent papers, and introduces an o1 comparison in Appendix F. Bibliography entries for some retained baselines, including Monkey and LAVT, disappear. The broad positioning around dual-system visual reasoning and interpretable chains of evidence remains stable.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 4, methods precede the literature review, and the method subsections are reorganized. Ethics and reproducibility material is duplicated into new main-text sections. Several results, ablation, qualitative-analysis, and conclusion paragraphs are rewritten, alongside substantial expansion of Appendix A.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Figure 4 comparison chart and Tables 6–7, extends Table 1, and changes headers, caption styling, and float placement for the conference format. Most existing visual designs are retained, including the method schematics, qualitative examples, failure panels, and structures of Tables 2–5.

improvement.justification: v3 makes training-data construction and the resampler substantially easier to inspect, while adding relevant comparators and diagnostics of the central switching claim. These improve reproducibility and empirical assessment. The gains remain limited by underspecified encoder and mode-comparison protocols, persistent switching figure/prose discrepancies, and Table 6's overbroad claim of superiority in both modes despite System 1 counterexamples. The net improvement is useful but limited.
